title: Widen tongue-and-groove pliers to the last groove: open wide, slide, close
instruction: The blue-handled tongue-and-groove pliers are set to their narrowest jaw, the first of five grooves. Reset them to the widest, the fifth groove, and leave them locked there, lying flat on the bench with nothing touching them.
context: Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (510,600 US jobs) and general maintenance and repair workers (1,621,800 US jobs in 2025; BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) use tongue-and-groove pliers on hose couplings and faucet nuts, and they are a common home toolbox tool. Before a grip, the joint is moved to the groove that fits the part; that reset is the task. The joint slides only with the handles 72 degrees or more apart, near their stop at 85. A reset is three moves in order: open wide, carry the joint 24 mm, close.
setup: Positions in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them. One pair of Channellock 420 straight-jaw tongue-and-groove pliers, 9.5 in long, 391 g, lies flat and loose on the bench top. Nothing else is on the bench and nothing is fixed. The handles are steel bars in a blue plastic dip; the head, jaws and rivet are bare steel. The two halves cross at the joint's rivet (a 10 mm round steel cap), which is at (0.380, 0.000). Both handles point back toward the robot: the slotted half's straight back, its centre line 18 mm left of the rivet, and the rivet half's 30 degrees to the right of it, so they start 30 degrees apart; the jaws point away and to the left. How the joint works: the slotted half carries a slot with five arc grooves, 6 mm apart (24 mm of travel), and the outer jaw; the rivet half, which lies on top, carries the rivet, a tongue that sits in one groove, and the inner jaw. The slot runs from the rivet back toward the robot and its left, 32 degrees off the slotted handle's line. Groove 1, at the slot's end nearest the jaws, is the narrowest jaw; groove 5, at its end nearest the handles, the widest. The pliers start in groove 1. With the handles less than 72 degrees apart the tongue stays in its groove: the handles turn about the rivet, but the joint cannot slide. From 72 degrees to the open stop at 85 the tongue is clear and the rivet slides along the slot. Closing below 72 drops the tongue into the nearest groove. With the handles closed the jaws touch in groove 1 and stand 6, 12, 18 and 24 mm apart in grooves 2 to 5. The layout is the same every trial.
scoring: Groove n: the rivet's centre within 1.5 mm of that groove's centre along the slot (real trial: the tongue seated in the nth groove from the jaw end). Locked: with the slotted half held, a 5 N push on the rivet half along the slot moves the rivet under 1 mm (the tongue is down in a groove: handles closed below the release angle, 72 degrees here). At rest: both halves lie flat on the bench (tilt under 3 degrees, lowest point within 2 mm of the bench top), and through the last 1 s both grippers stay at least 25 mm clear of the pliers (counted from the fingers' full sweep about the gripper's axis) while neither half nor the rivet moves more than 1 mm and neither half turns more than 1 degree. 1.0: locked in groove 5 and at rest. 0.5: locked in groove 2, 3 or 4 and at rest. 0.2: at some time the rivet slid at least 3 mm out of groove 1 with the handles open (72 degrees or more). 0: anything else, or any part of the pliers 5 cm or more below the bench top at the end (off the bench). Pliers left held, propped up or open at 72 degrees or more earn at most 0.2. Doing nothing scores 0. The trial ends once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Open the handles wide, slide the joint to the slot's end nearest the jaws (groove 1, the narrowest), close to 30 degrees and lay the pliers flat, rivet half on top: rivet at (0.380, 0.000), slotted half's handle straight back toward the arms, the other 30 degrees to its right. Check the joint will not slide.
fidelity: PhysX, 20 Hz. The joint: a 0 to 24 mm slider and a hinge (0 to 85 degrees). The lock is a rule on the handle spread: under 72 degrees a stiff spring holds the rivet in the groove it dropped into; above, it slides against joint friction set to 1.5 N and a drag, stiff past 22 mm/s. The halves do not collide; closing between grooves pulls it to the nearest groove (a real tongue may land on a ridge). Shapes are boxes. Release and stop angles, slide force and groove pitch are our estimates.
